correctness.rationale: For every prime p=8h+1>13 and r²≠4, a valuation-derived holomorphic basis of size six, explicit Cartier exponent selection, and characteristic-uniform polynomial identities prove that an invariant 2x2 coefficient block has determinant κ(r²−4)^{2h}≠0 and that a second scalar block is c(r²−4)^{2h}P_h. The remaining scalar blocks are P_h and twice Q_h. Since p≡1(mod8) each block is invariant and stable Cartier rank equals the stated geometric p-rank. The nonstandard identities follow from the displayed coefficient recurrences and polynomial ODE uniqueness; a standalone exact finite-prime checker separately reproduces identities and ranks. Finite checks do not replace the proof.

An aggregate mass formula cannot alone determine simultaneous zeros or exact rank of each parameter.

originality.rationale: The final claim is exact per-parameter p-rank and a universal nonvanishing Cartier determinant. Ohashi addresses superspeciality for the same curve, Bouw generic rank for wider cyclic covers, and Cavalieri–Pries aggregate nonordinary masses. Generic ordinarity, the family, the Cartier method, and mass/count formulas are credited to prior work, not claimed. No inspected comparison subsumes these two coefficient identities or the full special-fiber stratification; an old equivalent simplification remains a real priority risk.

value.rationale: Exact all-parameter p-rank equations for the genus-six order-eight family supply more information than generic ordinarity or superspeciality. The nonvanishing 2x2 Cartier block is a structural, uniform lower bound, and p=17 provides concrete rank-2, rank-4, and rank-6 strata; the exact special-fiber stratification is a natural precursor to finer Newton/Ekedahl–Oort questions.
